items.description:

items.title: Ireland men set for maiden tour of Pakistan in January, to play three ODIs
items.description:
The Ireland men’s team will tour Pakistan in January for the first time to play three One-day Internationals against the hosts, the cricket boards of both countries announced on Thursday.
The visitors, according to the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), are scheduled to arrive in the country on Jan 9, and will take on national developmental side Pakistan Shaheens for three warm-up one-day matches between Jan 13 and 17.

items.title: Govt to limit additional fuel cost charges to consumers at 83 paise per unit
items.description:
ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Thursday announced that it would limit additional fuel cost charges to consumers at 83 paise per unit (kWh) through a forward-looking adjustment on a quarterly basis, instead of Rs2.88 per unit in additional fuel cost it was seeking for December billing.
The Power Division, in a statement, said it has “proposed a Forward-looking Fuel Cost Adjustment (FFCA) mechanism wherein the increase … would be limited to approximately Rs0.83 per unit (inclusive of taxes) for the period October–December 2026” over the September FCA.

items.title: Police use tear gas to disperse fresh Bangladesh garment worker protests
items.description:
Bangladesh police said they fired tear gas shells and used sound grenades to disperse protesting garment workers who tried ​to block a major highway on Thursday to press ‌their demand for better wages.
The fresh protest broke out a day after a six-member panel approved a 36 per cent increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, ​the smallest in four decades, despite weeks of protests and calls ​for the sum to be doubled.

items.title: Security forces kill 12 India-sponsored terrorists in multiple IBOs in Balochistan: ISPR
items.description:
Security forces killed 12 India-sponsored terrorists in four separate intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan between November 20 and 23, the military’s media wing said on Thursday.
According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), security forces targeted a terrorist hideout in Nushki district on November 20. Following an intense exchange of fire, eight terrorists belonging to the Indian-backed Fitna-al-Hindustan were killed. Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the site, the ISPR added.
